article.headline: Williams, Roberts ignite No. 10 Texas Tech in 53-25 win over Arizona State

article.linkText: Williams, Roberts ignite No. 10 Texas Tech in 53-25 win over Arizona State

categories.description: Arizona State Sun Devils @ Texas Tech Red Raiders

event.description: Arizona State Sun Devils @ Texas Tech Red Raiders

keywords: Arizona State Sun Devils @ Texas Tech Red Raiders
article.story: LUBBOCK, Texas -- — J'Koby Williams ran for a career-high 165 yards with two long touchdowns after an early fumble, Ben Roberts returned an interception for a touchdown and No. 10 Texas Tech overwhelmed Arizona State 53-25 on Saturday in a matchup of the past two Big 12 champions. The reigning champion Red Raiders (6-0, 3-0 Big 12) broke a school record with their eighth consecutive regular-season conference victory since a 26-22 loss last year at Arizona State. Their 12th home win in a row is one short of the longest streak in school history set in 1942. Texas Tech led for good on Roberts' 24-yard pick-6, the fourth time in three games a Red Raiders linebacker returned an interception for a touchdown. That came three plays after Williams' fumble at the Sun Devils 2 on the 13th play of the game's opening possession. The Red Raiders scored on the last seven drives of the first half, with four TDs and three field goals by Stone Harrington (31, 42 and 37 yards) for a 43-10 halftime lead. They already had 404 of their 502 total yards by then. “That was something that was totally different,” coach Joey McGuire said. “We’ve been really slow starting and playing great in the second half. I was really excited the way we started. It wasn’t that we did anything different. We just executed better and played at a really high level.” Reed Harris had his Big 12-leading eighth TD catch for Arizona State (3-3, 1-2) on the first drive after halftime, on a 2-yard pass from backup Mikey Keene. Will Hammond, the starter for Tech in last year's game at Arizona State when Behren Morton was injured, completed 18 of 26 passes for 232 yards with an 11-yard TD to Coy Eakin. Hammond also had a 9-yard TD run. Kenny Johnson had seven catches for 120 yards. “Will grew today as a quarterback,” McGuire said. “He did some things today, extremely composed, that I haven’t seen. You’ve seen flashes. But I haven’t seen a half like that out of him.” Williams had only 11 carries and his two TD runs covered 100 yards. His 62-yard sprint down the left sideline put the Red Raiders up 21-0 in the first quarter, and he later added a 38-yard score when he went through a gap on the left side, got by one defender and then spun past another. Texas Tech was without Williams' backfield mate, Cameron Dickey, who has a high ankle sprain. “Everybody needs a J'Koby Williams in their life,” McGuire said. “He's just one of those guys that just lights up the room. He knew he had a lot on his shoulders not having Cam Dickey.” The takeaway Arizona State: While the loser in this game each of the past two seasons went on to win the Big 12 title, this Sun Devils team is reeling in conference play. They lost 55-19 at home to Baylor two weeks ago when they gave up 564 yards. Texas Tech: The Red Raiders are 18-2 since the start of the 2025 season, and 17 of those wins are by double-digits. They are 41-18 in coach Joey McGuire's five seasons with a 26-5 mark at home. Sun Devils QB switch Keene took over after halftime and completed 25 of 34 passes for 256 yards and two TDs. Kentucky transfer Cutter Boley was 5-of-10 passing in the first half with two interceptions and 124 yards — 74 of those on a TD to Raiden Vines-Bright. “I'm going to assess all personnel after I watch the tape on all phases,” coach Kenny Dillingham said. “But I was very, very happy with how Mikey went in, and I was very, very happy with Mikey's leadership and command and his veteran presence in that group.” Up next Arizona State is home against Kansas State next Saturday. Texas Tech travels to Cincinnati. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college football coverage here
